reply: You asked, 13:35 CST Nov 16: why couldn't cloud sessions refresh the live file, if the commits point at the roadmap branch that never goes to main? They can, and I did: this session (a cloud session) rebuilt the live file at 13:26 CST and pushed it to the roadmap branch (commit b8afbff390), with no PR and no CI. So the consultant's line "cloud sessions cannot refresh it" (relayed 11:00 CST, not measured by it) is wrong for a session like mine. What is true, measured today: a refresh is a manual job for a session. It took about 21 list_sessions pages (2,100 session rows), 12 pages of open PRs over GitHub REST, then a commit and push. No timer does it, so the file is stale between refreshes (the last one before today was 12:27 CST). build.py, which is Python, cannot call list_sessions at all. That makes option b real: keep the live file as the only source, committed to the roadmap branch, and the row reads UNKNOWN only when nobody has refreshed it. The cost is that someone must refresh it. The earlier note of yours ("just needs a table") fits option b. Options are unchanged; the item stays open for your pick.
